description: You opened and face a 3-bet: 4-bet (value+bluff) / call / fold, keyed by hero position x 3-bettor position. Value-heavy per low-stakes research; IP continues wider than OOP.

rationale_parts.lead: Your tight UTG open just got 3-bet (re-raised) by the button: continue only with the very top of your range and fold the rest.
points: 4-bet only KK+ and AKs — the hands still ahead of a range that can call your 4-bet.
Call with QQ, JJ, AKo and AQs to keep the pot controlled while out of position.
Everything else folds: live players 3-bet-bluff far less than theory says, so a 3-bet here is almost always a real hand.

rationale_parts.lead: You opened from an early seat and the button 3-bet (re-raised): continue only with the very top and fold everything else.
points: 4-bet only KK+ and AKs — the hands still ahead of a range that can call your 4-bet.
Call with QQ, JJ, AKo and AQs to keep the pot controlled while out of position.
The rest folds: live players under-3-bet-bluff, so their 3-bets are rarely light.

rationale_parts.lead: You opened the cutoff and the button 3-bet — you'll be out of position all hand, so defend a tighter, stronger set of hands.
points: 4-bet QQ+ and AK, plus A5s as the one bluff — its ace blocks (makes it less likely they hold) their strongest hands.
Call with 99–JJ, AQs, AJs and KQs: enough strength to continue, not enough to stack off (put your whole stack in).
Against players who rarely 3-bet-bluff, everything else folds instead of calling to get dominated.

rationale_parts.lead: You opened the cutoff and the small blind 3-bet: their range is heavy with real hands, but you'll have position — continue accordingly.
points: 4-bet QQ+ and AK, with A5s as the blocker bluff.
Call with TT, JJ, AQs, AJs and KQs — hands with the strength and playability to continue in position.
Fold the hands a value-heavy 3-bet range dominates — calling with them just pays off better hands.

actions.combos: 22-JJ, AQs, AJs, ATs, KQs, KJs, QJs, JTs, T9s, AQo

rationale_parts.lead: You opened the button and the big blind 3-bet — you'll have position on every street, so this is the spot to defend widest, not fold.
points: 4-bet QQ+ and AK, adding A5s and A4s as bluffs — their aces block the hands that can fight back.
Call with every pair 22–JJ, the suited Broadways, JTs/T9s and AQo: position lets these hands cash in their potential cheaply.

rationale_parts.lead: You opened the button and the small blind 3-bet: same in-position edge as against the big blind, but their range runs a touch stronger — trim slightly.
points: 4-bet QQ+ and AK with just one bluff (A5s).

Still call the wide block of pairs and suited Broadways (22–JJ, AQs–ATs, KQs–QJs, JTs, AQo) — they play profitably in position against a value-heavy 3-bettor; only the weakest connector (T9s) gets dropped.
